sources.title: Memory for Autonomous LLM Agents: Mechanisms, Evaluation, and Emerging Frontiers
sources.summary: Survey of agent memory mechanisms 2022–early 2026 covering five mechanism families, four benchmarks and five application domains, ending with an explicit list of open challenges.
key_facts: Open challenges named: continual consolidation, causally grounded retrieval, trustworthy reflection, learned forgetting, multimodal embodied memory.
Engineering challenges flagged: write-path filtering, contradiction handling, latency budgets, privacy governance.
Surveys five mechanism families, four recent benchmarks that 'reveal system gaps', five domains where memory is differentiating.
Domains where memory differentiates: personal assistants, coding agents, open-world games, scientific reasoning, multi-agent teamwork.

sources.title: A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents: Attacks, Defenses, and Governance Across the Memory Lifecycle (Toward Mnemonic Sovereignty)
sources.venue_or_author: Lin, Hao, Fu, Cui, Chen, Li, Li, Xiong (arXiv, Apr 2026, rev. Jun 2026)
sources.summary: Security survey that frames long-term memory threats as persistent, stateful and propagating, organizes them over a six-phase memory lifecycle, and argues security must be built in at storage time.
key_facts: Threat landscape defined by three properties: 'persistence, statefulness, and propagation'.
Memory Lifecycle Framework: six phases (Write, Store, Retrieve, Execute, Share & Propagate, Forget & Rollback), four objectives (Integrity, Confidentiality, Availability, Governance).
Claim: 'robust Long-Term Memory security cannot be retrofitted at retrieval or execution time alone'.
Proposes Verifiable Memory Governance (VMG) requiring five architectural primitives; security 'anchored in storage-time provenance, versioning, and policy-aware retention'.
Covers memory poisoning, injection, RAG corruption, memory extraction/privacy leakage, shared multi-agent memory, forgetting/unlearning.

sources.title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
sources.summary: Shows that summarization-based context compaction silently drops in-context governance constraints, causing agents to perform prohibited tool actions; introduces the ConstraintRot benchmark and a pinning mitigation.
key_facts: ConstraintRot benchmark: 1,323 episodes across seven model families with deterministic tool-call grading.
Violations rise from 0% with full policy context to 30% after compaction; up to 59% for some models.
When constraints survive summarization: 0% violations; when dropped: 38% violation rate.
Constraint Pinning (training-free) quarantines constraints from lossy compaction and restores violations to 0%.
Positions 'context management as a first-class governance surface for deployed LLM agents'.

sources.title: Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance
sources.venue_or_author: Kelly Hong, Anton Troynikov, Jeff Huber (Chroma)
sources.summary: Empirical study of 18 frontier models showing non-uniform performance degradation as input length grows, even on simple tasks, with stated gaps around mechanism and context construction.
key_facts: Published July 14, 2025; tested 18 LLMs including GPT-4.1, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3.
LongMemEval: focused inputs (~300 tokens) vs full inputs (~113k tokens); 'significantly higher performance on focused prompts' across all models.
Claude Opus 4 showed largest focused/full gap; degradation persists with thinking modes enabled.
Single distractor reduces performance; four distractors compound degradation; Claude lowest hallucination, GPT highest.
'Models perform worse when the haystack preserves a logical flow of ideas'; shuffled haystacks improved all 18 models.
Open questions: degradation mechanisms unexplained, need 'mechanistic interpretability'; context construction/management under-explored.

sources.title: Beyond a Million Tokens: Benchmarking and Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLMs (BEAM / LIGHT)
sources.venue_or_author: Tavakoli, Salemi, Ye, Abdalla, Zamani, Mitchell (arXiv, Oct 2025, rev. Feb 2026)
sources.summary: Introduces BEAM, a long-term memory benchmark with conversations up to 10M tokens, and LIGHT, a three-component memory framework; finds 1M-context models and retrieval both struggle as dialogues lengthen.
key_facts: BEAM: 100 conversations up to 10 million tokens, 2,000 validated questions, ten memory abilities.
'Even LLMs with 1M token context windows (with and without retrieval-augmentation) struggle as dialogues lengthen.'
Existing benchmarks 'often lack narrative coherence, cover narrow domains, and only test simple recall-oriented tasks'.
LIGHT = long-term episodic memory + short-term working memory + scratchpad of salient facts; +3.5%–12.69% over strongest baselines.

sources.title: Always-On Agents: A Survey of Persistent Memory, State, and Governance in LLM Agents
sources.summary: Survey of 435 works on persistent state in agents (memories, ledgers, permissions, credentials, provenance) that finds the field over-invests in accumulation/retrieval and under-invests in governing, recovering and relinquishing state.
key_facts: Coded corpus of 435 works; state evaluated on six axes: authority, scope, mutability, provenance, recoverability, actionability.
Finding: literature 'concentrates more heavily on accumulating and retrieving state than on governing, recovering, or relinquishing it'.
Calls for links to databases, distributed systems, formal methods, capability security, machine unlearning.
Proposes Always-On Evaluation Protocol (AOEP-v0) addressing 'state mutation and recovery obligations'.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Memory from a Computer Architecture Perspective: Visions and Challenges Ahead
sources.venue_or_author: Yu, Yu, Zhang, Ni, Yin, Yang, Zhao, Zhao (arXiv, Mar 2026)
sources.summary: Position paper reframing multi-agent memory as a computer-architecture problem with a three-layer hierarchy and shared vs distributed paradigms; names consistency as the most pressing open challenge.
key_facts: Proposes three-layer memory hierarchy (I/O, cache, memory) and shared vs distributed memory paradigms for agents.
Two protocol gaps identified: cache sharing across agents and structured memory access control.
'The most pressing open challenge is multi-agent memory consistency' (coherence/consistency analogues).

sources.title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
sources.summary: Formalizes context engineering (retrieval/generation, processing, management; RAG, memory, tool-integrated reasoning, multi-agent) from 1,300+ papers and names the comprehension-generation asymmetry as the central open gap.
key_facts: Systematic analysis of over 1,300 research papers; defines context engineering as a formal discipline beyond prompt design.
Core open challenge: comprehension-generation gap — models comprehend complex contexts but 'exhibit pronounced limitations in generating equally sophisticated, long-form outputs'.
Taxonomy: foundational components (retrieval/generation, processing, management) and system implementations (RAG, memory systems, tool-integrated reasoning, multi-agent).

sources.title: Memory Injection Attacks on LLM Agents via Query-Only Interaction (MINJA)
sources.summary: Demonstrates that an attacker can poison an agent's memory bank purely through queries and observed outputs, without store access, using bridging steps, an indication prompt and progressive shortening.
key_facts: 98.2% injection success rate and 76.8% attack success rate via query-only interaction.
Attack uses bridging steps, an indication prompt, and a progressive shortening strategy to plant malicious records.
Recommended defenses: memory isolation, strong user authentication, secure memory management, advanced prompt filtering.

sources.title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
sources.summary: 2026 follow-up to MINJA-style work studying both poisoning attacks and defenses for memory-based agents (details beyond title not retrieved).
key_facts: Jan 2026 arXiv paper pairing memory poisoning attacks with defenses for memory-based LLM agents (v2 available).

sources.title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents
sources.summary: Proposes anomaly detection for poisoned entries in retrieval-augmented agent memory, indicating defenses are moving toward store-side monitoring (details beyond title not retrieved).
key_facts: May 2026 defense paper targeting memory poisoning in retrieval-augmented agents via gradient-coupled anomaly detection.

sources.title: Parallel Context Compaction for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Serving
sources.summary: Treats compaction as a serving-systems problem: LLM summarization is lossy and blocking, so the paper runs compaction in parallel to bound summary volume and latency.
key_facts: 'Summarization is inherently lossy and the blocking call stalls agent inference for tens of seconds.'
Parallel compaction aims to give operators 'fine-grained, predictable control over summary volume'.

sources.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
sources.summary: Argues compaction inside RL training is underexplored and jointly trains task execution and summary generation so agents learn from compacted trajectories.
key_facts: 'Incorporating compaction into reinforcement learning remains underexplored.'
Method: token-level loss normalization plus cross-trajectory generalized advantage estimation over compacted rollouts.

sources.title: Addressable Recall Compaction for Long Context-Window Control in AI Agents (ARC)
sources.summary: Proposes lossless compaction via addressable pointers and on-demand recall, claiming it beats summarization- and RAG-based compaction on context-overflow failures.
key_facts: Existing compaction (discard/summarize/retrieve) 'may remove task-critical details or fail to recover them reliably'.
ARC: addressable pointers + on-demand recall; outperforms summarization- and RAG-based baselines on overflow prevention.

sources.title: Agentic Unlearning: When LLM Agent Meets Machine Unlearning
sources.summary: Shows sensitive information persists in both model parameters and external memory stores, so deletion must be synchronized across both to prevent recontamination.
key_facts: Problem: information 'backflow' — unlearned data re-enters via the other pathway (parameters vs external memory).
Proposes Synchronized Backflow Unlearning (SBU), a dual-pathway framework coordinating parametric and memory-store forgetting.

sources.title: MemLeak: Diagnosing Information Leaks in Multimodal Agent Memory
sources.summary: Diagnoses information leakage from multimodal long-term agent memory and introduces a benchmark (Mem-Gallery) for multimodal conversational memory.
key_facts: Introduces Mem-Gallery benchmark for multimodal long-term conversational memory in MLLM agents.
Frames privacy leakage from stored multimodal memory as an open diagnostic problem.

sources.title: Control-Plane Placement Shapes Forgetting: An Architectural Study of Agent Memory Across Thirteen System Configurations
sources.summary: Empirical architecture study showing that where the memory control plane sits changes what the agent forgets, across thirteen configurations.
key_facts: Compares thirteen agent-memory system configurations; control-plane placement is a determinant of forgetting behaviour.

sources.title: Governing Evolving Memory in LLM Agents: Risks, Mechanisms, and the Stability and Safety Governed Memory (SSGM) Framework
sources.summary: Frames self-evolving agent memory as a governance risk and proposes the SSGM framework for stability and safety of memory evolution.
key_facts: Mar 2026 framework paper treating evolving memory as a risk surface requiring stability and safety governance (SSGM).

sources.title: AI Memory Benchmarks 2026: LoCoMo, LongMemEval & BEAM
sources.summary: Vendor explainer of the three dominant memory benchmarks with Mem0's self-reported scores; concedes LoCoMo's limitations but does not mention the DMR benchmark.
key_facts: LongMemEval: 500 questions; five abilities incl. abstention; LongMemEval_S ~115k tokens/~40 sessions, _M ~500 sessions.
LoCoMo: 1,540 questions (single-hop, multi-hop, open-domain, temporal).
LoCoMo limits per Mem0: 'average context length is modest by 2026 standards' and 'does not explicitly score knowledge updates'.
Mem0 self-reported: LoCoMo 92.5%, LongMemEval 94.4%, BEAM-1M 62%, 6.7K–7.0K tokens per retrieval.
No mention of DMR benchmark or Zep/Mem0 dispute on this page.

sources.title: Your 1M Context Window Is Lying: What Chroma's Context Rot Study Proves
sources.venue_or_author: Particula (practitioner blog; figures per search digest of context-rot cluster)
sources.summary: Practitioner synthesis of Chroma, RULER and NoLiMa findings arguing advertised windows overstate usable context; RULER/NoLiMa numbers below came from the search digest of this result cluster, not a direct fetch.
key_facts: RULER: effective context defined as longest input above fixed quality threshold; 17 models tested.
RULER: Yi-34B 200K claimed, 32K effective (16%); GPT-4 128K claimed, 64K effective (50%); effective ~50–65% of advertised.
NoLiMa: at 32K tokens, 11 of 13 models fell below half their short-context score; GPT-4o 99.3% to 69.7%.

sources.title: Agent Memory Architectures: Vector, Graph & Episodic
sources.venue_or_author: SandBase blog (practitioner; attribution per search digest)
sources.summary: Practitioner comparison of vector, graph and episodic memory trade-offs, claiming production agents in 2026 layer all three.
key_facts: 'Vector memory is fast and cheap but forgets relationships; graph memory captures structure but adds 200-400ms per lookup.'
Episodic buffers keep temporal order but 'blow up your context window'; 2026 production agents layer vector+graph+episodic.
Multiple agents needing consistent entity views is cited as the trigger for adding a shared memory layer.

sources.title: [Memory]: Defend against memory injection attacks (vllm-project/semantic-router issue #1386)
sources.summary: Open-source router project tracking MINJA-style memory injection as a defense requirement, indicating memory security has reached infra maintainers' backlogs.
key_facts: Issue in vllm-project/semantic-router explicitly scopes defending against memory injection attacks in the memory module.

sources.title: Context Is Not Comprehension
sources.summary: Argues that long-context recall benchmarks do not measure comprehension, supporting the case that effective context must be measured on reasoning tasks rather than retrieval.
key_facts: Surfaced alongside the Mei survey as foundational to the claim that context length ≠ comprehension.

sources.title: Evaluating Memory Condensation Strategies for Coding Agents in Data-Driven Scientific Discovery
sources.summary: Evaluates condensation/compaction strategies specifically for coding agents on long scientific-discovery tasks, a domain-specific angle on compaction information loss.
key_facts: May 2026 empirical comparison of memory condensation strategies for coding agents in data-driven scientific discovery.

sources.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
sources.summary: Early work training agents with RL to decide memory add/update/delete operations, a precursor to the 2026 wave (Mem-T, DeferMem, CompactionRL) of learned memory management.
key_facts: Uses RL to learn memory management (add/update/delete) and utilization rather than hand-written heuristics.

notes: Searched: memory benchmarks (LongMemEval/LoCoMo/MemBench/BEAM), context rot (Chroma/RULER/NoLiMa), compaction information loss, MINJA/memory injection, agent-memory surveys and future directions, Mei et al. context-engineering survey, KG-vs-vector and multi-agent shared memory, forgetting/unlearning/privacy.
